system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The only verified input says there is no nuclear incident: this is a routine practice alert meant for the training system. The alert, however, is marked Actual, Observed and Severe, and its description says an incident was reported at Pickering. That repeats the January 2020 false-alert pattern. A person must stop this from going out live and confirm it goes only to the training system as an exercise. The drafter cannot fix this simply by editing fields.

objections.issue: Status is Actual for what the verified input and context describe as a shift-change practice alert meant for the training system. Actual means every targeted member of the public is expected to act.
objections.fix: A person must confirm that this goes only to the Alert Ready training system and not to the live system. If any CAP message is produced, it must use status Exercise and put the exercise identifier in the note.

evidence.quote: Actionable only by designated exercise participants; exercise identifier should appear in <note>
meant for the Alert Ready training system
believed they had switched to the training system, selected a pre-scripted nuclear template for the PNGS and accidentally sent a live alert

objections.issue: Certainty Observed, together with Severe and Immediate, asserts a nuclear incident that has occurred or is ongoing. No verified input supports any hazard; the verified record says there was no information about any nuclear incident.
objections.fix: Do not issue any live hazard assertion. Severity, urgency and certainty must not claim an observed incident when no hazard bulletin supports one.

was not acting on any information concerning any nuclear incident

objections.issue: The description states as fact that an incident was reported at Pickering and that emergency staff are responding. No verified input contains any such report; this is pre-scripted template text.
objections.fix: Remove the incident claims and the claim that emergency staff are responding. Any exercise text must be clearly marked as an exercise and never sent to the public.
